newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ex-Aquino aide called "God's choice" for president.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Aquino aide called "God's choice" for president.

text.p: The Philippines' 68 million people will have to wait until next year to learn who will be their next president, but a Christian revival group says God has already decided.

In a ceremony -- bizarre even for this largely Roman Catholic country where cults abound -- a preacher on Tuesday poured oil over the head of Aquilino Pimentel, a top aide of former president Corazon Aquino, and said he was God's choice.
"The Lord has called you to serve as the next president of this country," said evangelist Willie Nakar of the National Renewal Movement (NRM). "Do you accept?"
"Not my will but His be done. I accept," said Pimentel as he knelt before an image of Jesus Christ, an NRM official told Reuters on Thursday.

Pimentel, 63, was jailed four times by the late president Ferdinand Marcos for alleged rebellious activities. He was Aquino's secretary for local governments in 1986 and was elected senator in 1987, but lost in his vice presidential bid in 1992.

More than a dozen politicians have expressed interest in succeeding President Fidel Ramos, whose six-year term ends next year. The constitution limits presidents to one term. Pimentel's political platform calls for eradicating poverty and abolishing personal and corporate taxes.
Asked how he would run his government without collecting taxes, Pimentel said: "God has other means."
